47670.q: Which later reformer, as General Secretary of the Central Committee’s Secretariat, played a leading role in the Anti-Rightist Campaign in 1957?
47670.e: As head of the Central Committee’s Secretariat, Deng Xiaoping organised the campaign against the “rightists”. After 1978 many of those affected were rehabilitated.
47670.m: The later reformer Deng Xiaoping also took part in the Anti-Rightist Campaign.

47671.q: According to official figures, how many people were labelled “rightists” in the campaign after the Hundred Flowers Campaign?
47671.e: The official figure is about 550,000 people, and some historians’ estimates are higher. Most were later rehabilitated.
47671.m: After 1957 hundreds of thousands were persecuted as “rightists”.

47672.q: Who mainly made up the Red Guards of the Cultural Revolution?
47672.e: The first Red Guards appeared in spring 1966 at Beijing secondary schools and universities. Mao used the young people against his opponents in the party.
47672.m: The Red Guards were mainly young school pupils and students.

47673.q: During which political campaign did the Red Guards appear?
47673.e: The Cultural Revolution lasted from 1966 to 1976. The Red Guards shaped mainly its first years.
47673.m: The Red Guards were the shock troops of the Cultural Revolution.

47674.q: Which “Four Olds” were the Red Guards supposed to attack?
a: Old ideas, old culture, old customs, old habits
Old emperors, old temples, old books, old coins
Old landlords, old officials, old traders, old priests
Old laws, old taxes, old borders, old treaties
47674.e: In the fight against the “Four Olds”, Red Guards destroyed temples, works of art and books and humiliated teachers and intellectuals.
47674.m: The Red Guards were meant to smash old ideas, culture, customs and habits.

47675.q: Where did Mao Zedong receive millions of Red Guards at mass rallies from August 1966?
a: In the People’s Palace in Shanghai
In front of the Presidential Palace in Nanjing
47675.e: Mao appeared at eight rallies in Tiananmen Square. In total about 11 to 13 million young people are said to have taken part.
47675.m: In Tiananmen Square millions of Red Guards cheered Mao.

47676.q: How were the Red Guards largely broken up from 1968?
a: By being sent to the countryside
By being called up to fight in Korea
Through elections to the People’s Congress
47676.e: After the Red Guards had fought one another in bloody factional battles, the leadership sent millions of young people “up to the mountains and down to the villages”.
47676.m: From 1968 the Red Guards were sent to work in the countryside.

47677.q: Which book did the Red Guards often carry as a sign of recognition?
a: The “Little Red Book” of Mao quotations
47677.e: “Quotations from Chairman Mao Tse-tung” was printed in huge numbers. Red Guards waved the little red book at rallies and learnt quotations by heart.
47677.m: The “Little Red Book” was the Red Guards’ sign of recognition.

47678.q: Which senior politician, then head of state, was attacked by Red Guards in the Cultural Revolution and died in custody in 1969?
47678.e: Liu Shaoqi was persecuted as a “capitalist roader”, expelled from the party in 1968 and died in 1969 without proper medical treatment. He was rehabilitated in 1980.
47678.m: Head of state Liu Shaoqi became the most prominent victim of the Cultural Revolution.

47679.q: Which term for enemies appears in a famous Mao quotation in the Little Red Book?
47679.e: Mao called the imperialists and all reactionaries “paper tigers”. They seemed frightening, he said, but were really weak.
47679.m: According to Mao, all reactionaries are paper tigers.

47680.q: How does a famous Mao quotation about revolution in the Little Red Book continue: “A revolution is not a ...”?
47680.e: The quotation comes from Mao’s 1927 report on the peasant movement in Hunan. It stresses that revolution is an act of violence.
47680.m: For Mao, a revolution was not a dinner party.

47681.q: Which defence minister promoted the Little Red Book and wrote its foreword?
47681.e: Lin Biao deliberately built up the personality cult around Mao. For a time he was seen as Mao’s successor, but he died in a plane crash in Mongolia in 1971.
47681.m: Lin Biao promoted the Mao cult with the collection of quotations.

47682.q: What happened to Lin Biao’s foreword in the Little Red Book after his death in 1971?
a: It was removed from many copies
It was printed on all banknotes
47682.e: After dying while fleeing, Lin Biao was regarded as a traitor. Owners tore out the foreword or blacked out his name.
47682.m: After Lin Biao’s fall, his foreword disappeared from the Little Red Book.

47683.q: Which famous Mao quotation about power is in the Little Red Book?
a: Political power grows out of the barrel of a gun
All power comes from the people
Power corrupts, absolute power corrupts absolutely
47683.e: Mao put this sentence into words in 1927, stressing the role of armed revolution. The other quotations come from other authors or from constitutions.
47683.m: According to Mao, political power grows out of the barrel of a gun.

47684.q: Why was the Little Red Book so small?
a: It was meant to fit in a uniform pocket
Large books were seen as bourgeois
It was only meant for children
47684.e: The handy size allowed soldiers, and later all citizens, to carry the book with them at all times.
47684.m: The Little Red Book fitted in any pocket.

47685.q: Which political phenomenon did the mass distribution of the Little Red Book strengthen?
47685.e: Mao was revered as an infallible leader, and his words were treated as the answer to every question. After his death the party officially criticised this cult.
47685.m: The Little Red Book was a tool of the personality cult.

47686.q: Who belonged to the Gang of Four as Mao Zedong’s wife?
47686.e: Jiang Qing was a former actress and Mao’s fourth wife. In the Cultural Revolution she controlled mainly art and culture.
47686.m: Mao’s wife Jiang Qing led the Gang of Four.

47687.q: When was the Gang of Four arrested?
47687.e: About a month after Mao’s death in September 1976, the new leadership had the four politicians arrested. This is seen as the end of the Cultural Revolution.
47687.m: The Gang of Four was toppled shortly after Mao’s death in 1976.

47688.q: Which person did NOT belong to the Gang of Four?
47688.e: The Gang of Four consisted of Jiang Qing, Zhang Chunqiao, Yao Wenyuan and Wang Hongwen. Hua Guofeng, as Mao’s successor, was involved in their arrest.
47688.m: Hua Guofeng was not part of the Gang of Four; he had them arrested.

47689.q: Which city was seen as the power base of the Gang of Four?
47689.e: Zhang Chunqiao, Yao Wenyuan and Wang Hongwen had begun their rise in Shanghai. The criticism that started the Cultural Revolution was also launched from there in 1965.
47689.m: The Gang of Four had its power base in Shanghai.

47690.q: When did the show trial of the Gang of Four take place?
47690.e: The trial was shown on television. Among other things, Jiang Qing defended herself by saying she had only followed Mao’s orders.
47690.m: The Gang of Four stood trial in 1980 and 1981.

47691.q: What sentence was Jiang Qing first given at the trial of the Gang of Four?
47691.e: The death sentence with a two-year reprieve was changed to life imprisonment in 1983. Jiang Qing died in 1991.
47691.m: Jiang Qing was sentenced to death, but the sentence was changed to life imprisonment.

47692.q: Which political direction did the Gang of Four stand for?
a: Radical supporters of the Cultural Revolution
Supporters of closer ties with the Soviet Union
47692.e: The Gang of Four drove the Cultural Revolution forward and fought moderate forces such as Deng Xiaoping. An article by its member Yao Wenyuan is seen as the start of the Cultural Revolution.
47692.m: The Gang of Four stood for the radical course of the Cultural Revolution.

47693.q: Who pushed through the policy of reform and opening up in China from 1978?
47693.e: After Mao’s death in 1976, Deng Xiaoping came out on top in the party. From December 1978 he put economic development at the centre instead of class struggle.
47693.m: Deng Xiaoping launched the policy of reform and opening up in 1978.

47694.q: Which four areas did the “Four Modernisations” cover?
a: Agriculture, industry, national defence, science and technology
47694.e: Zhou Enlai had already set out the goal. After 1978 Deng Xiaoping made the Four Modernisations the core of policy.
47694.m: The Four Modernisations covered agriculture, industry, defence, and science and technology.

47695.q: What did the household responsibility system introduce in farming?
a: Farming families could sell surpluses above a delivery quota themselves
All farms were merged into people’s communes
The state bought back all farmland
Farmers were given factory work in the cities
47695.e: Farmers leased land, delivered a fixed amount to the state and could sell the rest themselves. Harvests then rose considerably.
47695.m: The household responsibility system gave farming families an incentive to produce more.

47696.q: What did Deng Xiaoping mean with his saying about the black cat and the white cat?
a: What matters is usefulness, not ideology
Capitalism and socialism are the same
Farming is more important than industry
47696.e: Deng said, roughly, that it does not matter whether a cat is black or white as long as it catches mice. He put pragmatism above ideological purity.
47696.m: Deng Xiaoping’s cat saying stands for economic pragmatism.

47697.q: Which guiding principle of Deng Xiaoping justified growing income gaps during the reforms?
a: He who does not work shall not eat
47697.e: Deng assumed that some regions and people would go ahead and others would follow later. The coastal regions benefited first.
47697.m: Deng wanted some to get rich first.

47698.q: In which year did China join the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
47698.e: China joined on 11 December 2001 after years of negotiations. Membership sped up China’s rise to become an export power.
47698.m: China has been a member of the WTO since 2001.

47699.q: What are areas like Shenzhen called, where China allowed foreign companies under special rules from 1980?
47699.e: In the special economic zones taxes were lower and companies had more freedom. Shenzhen grew from a fishing village into a city of millions.
47699.m: Special economic zones opened China to foreign companies.

47700.q: Which island was declared a special economic zone as a whole province in 1988?
47700.e: In 1988 Hainan was separated from Guangdong and became a province of its own. At the same time it was given special economic zone status.
47700.m: Since 1988 Hainan has been a province and a special economic zone.

47701.q: What did the expression “Shenzhen speed” stand for in the 1980s?
a: The speed of China’s first express trains
The long working hours in Hong Kong
47701.e: While the International Trade Centre was being built, at times one floor was finished every three days. This became a symbol of Shenzhen’s development.
47701.m: “Shenzhen speed” stands for the city’s rapid development.

47702.q: Which slogan from Shenzhen became a symbol of the new business mentality in the 1980s?
a: Time is money, efficiency is life
47702.e: From 1981 the slogan was displayed on a board in the Shekou industrial area. At the time it was controversial because it sounded capitalist.
47702.m: “Time is money, efficiency is life” became Shenzhen’s motto.

47703.q: Which city was NOT one of China’s first four special economic zones of 1980?
47703.e: The first special economic zones were Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou and Xiamen. Shanghai only received similar special rights later.
47703.m: The first four special economic zones were all on the southern coast.

47704.q: Which area of Shanghai was developed from 1990 on the model of the special economic zones?
47704.e: Pudong, on the east bank of the Huangpu, was then mainly farmland. Today the Lujiazui financial district with its skyscrapers stands there.
47704.m: Pudong is Shanghai’s counterpart to the Shenzhen special economic zone.

47705.q: Which city got a stock exchange in 1990, at almost the same time as Shenzhen?
47705.e: The Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges both opened at the end of 1990. They stand for China opening up to the market economy.
47705.m: In 1990 Shanghai and Shenzhen got the first stock exchanges of the People’s Republic.

47706.q: Where does a large part of Shenzhen’s population come from?
a: They moved there from other provinces
They were resettled from Hong Kong
They have lived there for centuries
47706.e: Millions of migrant workers moved to Shenzhen for factory jobs. Many of them have no local household registration (hukou) there.
47706.m: Shenzhen is a city of newcomers.

47707.q: Which exception applied in many rural areas under the one-child policy?
a: A second child was allowed if the first was a girl
Farmers could have as many children as they liked
A second child was only allowed for boys
47707.e: Because sons were seen as workers and as support in old age, the rule was relaxed in the countryside. People also speak of a “one-and-a-half-child policy”.
47707.m: In the countryside families could often have a second child if the first was a girl.

47708.q: Which relaxation of the one-child policy was decided in 2013?
a: Couples could have two children if one parent was an only child
All couples could have three children
Only city dwellers could have two children
47708.e: Before that, this only applied if both parents were only children. The change was a first step away from the one-child policy.
47708.m: In 2013 the one-child policy was clearly relaxed for the first time.

47709.q: In which areas of China did the one-child policy never apply?
47709.e: The two special administrative regions have their own laws. The mainland’s family planning rules did not apply there.
47709.m: The one-child policy did not apply in Hong Kong and Macau.

47710.q: What were children called in China who were not officially registered because of the one-child policy?
47710.e: Without an entry in the household registration, these children had hardly any access to schools and health care. Their number was estimated at several million.
47710.m: Unregistered children in China had hardly any rights.

47711.q: What benefits did families with a one-child certificate receive?
a: Bonuses and priority access to services
Exemption from military service for all relatives
47711.e: Parents who committed to one child received, depending on the place, cash payments and advantages with housing, schools or pensions.
47711.m: The one-child policy worked with rewards and penalties.

47712.q: What does the “4-2-1” family structure, seen as a result of the one-child policy, describe?
a: Four grandparents, two parents, one child
Four children, two parents, one grandmother
Four rooms, two floors, one house
Four working days, two rest days, one holiday
47712.e: An only child may later have to support two parents and four grandparents. This makes the problems of an ageing society worse.
47712.m: In the 4-2-1 structure one child is responsible for six older relatives.

47713.q: How did the authorities enforce the one-child policy on families?
a: With heavy fines, pressure and sometimes force
With a ban on marriage for everyone
47713.e: Local authorities had to meet birth quotas. Families with too many children faced heavy fines and losing their jobs, and there were also serious human rights violations.
47713.m: The one-child policy was partly enforced by force.

47714.q: Which Chinese politician developed the principle of “one country, two systems”?
47714.e: Deng Xiaoping set out the idea in the early 1980s. It was meant to make reunification possible with areas that had a different economic system.
47714.m: Deng Xiaoping came up with “one country, two systems”.

47715.q: When was Hong Kong handed back to China by Great Britain?
47715.e: The handover ended about 150 years of British colonial rule. Hong Kong became a special administrative region.
47715.m: Hong Kong returned to China in 1997.

47716.q: Which territory did Portugal hand back to China in 1999?
47716.e: On 20 December 1999 Macau became a special administrative region of the People’s Republic. It was the last European colony in Asia.
47716.m: Since 1999 Macau has been a Chinese special administrative region.

47717.q: According to the agreement, for how many years after the handover should Hong Kong’s system stay unchanged?
47717.e: The Joint Declaration guaranteed Hong Kong its capitalist system and way of life until 2047.
47717.m: Hong Kong’s special status was promised for 50 years.

47718.q: Which 1984 agreement set out the handover of Hong Kong?
47718.e: Margaret Thatcher and Zhao Ziyang signed the declaration in December 1984. It laid down the principle of “one country, two systems” for Hong Kong.
47718.m: The 1984 Joint Declaration set the conditions for Hong Kong’s handover.

47719.q: What is the “mini-constitution” of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region called?
47719.e: The Basic Law came into force on 1 July 1997. Among other things, it sets out Hong Kong’s own courts, currency and administration.
47719.m: With the Basic Law, Hong Kong has its own mini-constitution.

47720.q: What were the 2014 protests in Hong Kong for free elections called, after a symbol used by the demonstrators?
47720.e: The demonstrators protected themselves with umbrellas against police pepper spray and tear gas. They demanded free elections for the head of government.
47720.m: The 2014 Umbrella Movement fought for free elections in Hong Kong.

47721.q: What happened to Xi Jinping’s father Xi Zhongxun during the Mao era?
a: He was toppled and persecuted for years
47721.e: Xi Zhongxun was a veteran of the revolution and a vice premier, but he was toppled in 1962 and persecuted in the Cultural Revolution. He was only rehabilitated after Mao’s death.
47721.m: Xi Jinping comes from a family of senior party officials.

47722.q: At which university did Xi Jinping study from 1975?
47722.e: Xi was admitted as a “worker-peasant-soldier student” and studied chemical engineering. Tsinghua University is in Beijing.
47722.m: Xi Jinping studied at Tsinghua University.

47723.q: Whom did Xi Jinping succeed as General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party?
47723.e: Hu Jintao had led the party from 2002 to 2012. The handover took place after the 18th Party Congress.
47723.m: Xi Jinping succeeded Hu Jintao at the head of the party.

47724.q: What happened to Xi Jinping at the 20th Party Congress of the Chinese Communist Party in October 2022?
a: He received a third term as General Secretary
He stepped down as General Secretary
He was expelled from the Politburo
47724.e: With this Xi broke the rule, usual since the 1990s, of two terms at the head of the party.
47724.m: In 2022 Xi Jinping began his third term as party leader.

47725.q: Which post did Xi Jinping hold in 2007, shortly before rising to the Politburo Standing Committee?
47725.e: Before that Xi had been party leader of Zhejiang province and governor of Fujian. After a few months in Shanghai he became a member of the Standing Committee at the end of 2007.
47725.m: Xi Jinping rose to the top via Fujian, Zhejiang and Shanghai.

47726.q: Which political slogan did Xi Jinping coin from 2012 for the rebirth of the nation?
47726.e: The “Chinese Dream” stands for the goal of leading the nation back to greatness and prosperity. Xi presented it shortly after taking office.
47726.m: The “Chinese Dream” is one of Xi Jinping’s key slogans.

47727.q: Apart from the party and the state, which chairmanship does Xi Jinping hold that gives him supreme command of the army?
a: Chairmanship of the Central Military Commission
Chairmanship of the Supreme People’s Court
Chairmanship of the Political Consultative Conference
47727.e: The Central Military Commission commands the People’s Liberation Army. Xi has led the party commission since 2012 and the state commission since 2013.
47727.m: As Chairman of the Central Military Commission, Xi commands the army.

47728.q: How many members has the Politburo Standing Committee had since 2012?
47728.e: From 2002 to 2012 the body had nine members. Since the 18th Party Congress it has had seven.
47728.m: The Politburo Standing Committee has seven members.

47729.q: What role does the Politburo Standing Committee play in China’s political system?
a: It is the party’s highest centre of power and so the country’s
It is an advisory body without power to decide
It is the country’s highest court
It only organises the party congresses
47729.e: The most important decisions are made in the small circle of the Standing Committee. Because the party leads the state, it is in effect China’s centre of power.
47729.m: The Politburo Standing Committee is China’s real centre of power.

47730.q: Which body formally elects the Politburo Standing Committee?
a: The Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party
47730.e: After each party congress, the new Central Committee elects the Politburo and the Standing Committee at its first plenary session. The choice is agreed beforehand at the top of the party.
47730.m: The Central Committee formally elects the Politburo and its Standing Committee.

47731.q: Who has been Premier of China since March 2023, and as such a member of the Politburo Standing Committee?
47731.e: Li Qiang was previously party leader of Shanghai. He succeeded Li Keqiang as head of government.
47731.m: Li Qiang has been Premier of China since 2023.

47732.q: How often is the Party Congress of the Chinese Communist Party held, after which the Standing Committee is newly chosen?
47732.e: The 20th Party Congress took place in October 2022, the 19th in 2017. After each one, the party leadership is newly appointed.
47732.m: The Chinese Communist Party’s congress meets every five years.

47733.q: How does the Standing Committee relate to the Politburo of the Chinese Communist Party?
a: It is a small inner circle within the Politburo
It is larger than the Politburo
It is a court that supervises the Politburo
It is a parliamentary committee with no link to the party
47733.e: The Politburo has about two dozen members. The seven members of the Standing Committee belong to it and form its most powerful core.
47733.m: The Politburo is much larger than its Standing Committee.

47734.q: What does the order of the members in the Politburo Standing Committee mean?
a: It shows their rank in the power hierarchy
It is drawn by lot every year
47734.e: The General Secretary is in first place, and the Premier is usually second. The order at public appearances reflects rank.
47734.m: The order in the Standing Committee shows political rank.

47735.q: How often does China’s National People’s Congress meet in full session?
47735.e: The roughly 3,000 delegates meet every March for about a week. In between, the Standing Committee does the work.
47735.m: The National People’s Congress meets once a year.

47736.q: Who has been President of the People’s Republic of China since 2013, elected to this post by the National People’s Congress?
47736.e: The People’s Congress elects the President. Xi Jinping was elected in 2013 and confirmed in 2018 and 2023. He is also head of the Communist Party.
47736.m: Xi Jinping is elected President by the People’s Congress.

47737.q: Which rule did the National People’s Congress remove from the Chinese constitution in 2018?
a: The limit of two terms for the presidency
The requirement for a popular vote for President
47737.e: With the 2018 change, Xi Jinping can stay President without limit. Critics saw it as a step towards one-man rule.
47737.m: Since 2018 the Chinese President’s term has no longer been limited.

47738.q: How are the delegates of the National People’s Congress elected?
a: Indirectly by the provincial people’s congresses
47738.e: The people’s congresses of the provinces, autonomous regions and directly governed cities elect the delegates. The army and Hong Kong and Macau also send representatives.
47738.m: The National People’s Congress is elected indirectly.

47739.q: How does the Chinese constitution describe the National People’s Congress?
a: As the highest organ of state power
As an advisory body of experts
As a second chamber alongside the Senate
47739.e: Formally, the government, courts and President are below the People’s Congress. In reality the Communist Party decides policy.
47739.m: According to the constitution, the People’s Congress is the highest state body.

47740.q: Which speech traditionally opens the annual session of the National People’s Congress?
a: The government work report by the Premier
The report of the Supreme People’s Court
The speech of the army chief
47740.e: In the work report the Premier reviews the past year and names targets, such as the planned economic growth.
47740.m: The Premier opens the session with the government report.

47741.q: Where does China’s National People’s Congress meet?
a: In the Great Hall of the People in Beijing
In the Government Palace in Shanghai
In the Forbidden City in Nanjing
47741.e: The Great Hall of the People stands on Tiananmen Square in Beijing. The annual sessions take place there.
47741.m: The People’s Congress meets in the Great Hall of the People in Beijing.

47742.q: Which politician coined the term “socialism with Chinese characteristics” in 1982?
47742.e: Deng used the phrase in his speech to the 12th Party Congress in 1982. It justified market reforms under party leadership.
47742.m: The term “socialism with Chinese characteristics” comes from Deng Xiaoping.

47743.q: Which economic model did the 14th Party Congress set as the goal in 1992?
a: Free market economy without the state
47743.e: The market was to allocate resources, while the party and state companies controlled key sectors. In 1993 the goal was written into the constitution.
47743.m: China calls its system a socialist market economy.

47744.q: How does the Chinese Communist Party describe China’s stage of development in terms of socialism with Chinese characteristics?
a: As the primary stage of socialism
47744.e: The theory, set out at the 13th Party Congress in 1987, says China must first develop its productive forces. Market elements are therefore needed for the time being.
47744.m: According to the party, China is in the primary stage of socialism.

47745.q: Which is NOT one of the “Four Cardinal Principles” that Deng Xiaoping laid down in 1979?
a: A multi-party system on the western model
47745.e: The Four Cardinal Principles set political limits on reform: the socialist road, the people’s democratic dictatorship, party leadership, and Marxism-Leninism and Mao Zedong Thought.
47745.m: The Four Cardinal Principles secure the rule of the Communist Party.

47746.q: Which group was officially allowed to join the Chinese Communist Party from 2001?
47746.e: With his theory of the “Three Represents”, Jiang Zemin opened the party to entrepreneurs. They used to be seen as class enemies, whereas workers, farmers and soldiers had always been allowed.
47746.m: Since 2001 entrepreneurs have also been allowed to join the Chinese Communist Party.

47747.q: Which goal of a “moderately prosperous society” did the party leadership declare achieved in 2021?
47747.e: Xiaokang means a society with modest prosperity. On the party’s 100th anniversary, Xi Jinping announced that the goal had been reached.
47747.m: Xiaokang stands for a moderately prosperous society.

47748.q: Which problems did Hu Jintao mainly want to tackle with his guiding idea of more balanced development?
a: The gap between town and country and environmental damage
The lack of factories in the cities
Too much dependence on the Soviet Union
47748.e: After decades of rapid growth the coastal cities were rich, the countryside stayed poor and the environment suffered. Hu Jintao’s “Scientific Outlook on Development” was meant to balance this out.
47748.m: Hu Jintao wanted to make growth fairer and more environmentally friendly.

47749.q: Which natural obstacles did the Red Army have to overcome in western China in 1935?
47749.e: The troops crossed passes more than 4,000 metres high and the marshy grasslands on the border with Tibet. Many died of cold, hunger and exhaustion.
47749.m: Snowy mountains and marshes were among the hardest parts of the Long March.

47750.q: Which concept by Mao from 1940 described the political system of the first years after the founding of the state?
47750.e: According to Mao, an alliance of several classes under communist leadership was to govern at first. The transition to socialism followed from 1953.
47750.m: New Democracy was Mao’s model for the early years of the People’s Republic.

47751.q: Who founded the Việt Minh in 1941 as an alliance for Vietnamese independence?
47751.e: Hồ Chí Minh founded the Việt Minh in 1941 after returning to Vietnam. The organisation was led by communists but also brought together non-communist nationalists.
47751.m: Hồ Chí Minh founded the Việt Minh in 1941.

47752.q: What does the full name of the “Việt Minh” mean in translation?
a: League for the Independence of Vietnam
People’s Army of the Republic of Vietnam
National Front for a United Asia
47752.e: The full name is Việt Nam Độc Lập Đồng Minh Hội, meaning League for the Independence of Vietnam. The name stressed the national goal, not communism.
47752.m: The Việt Minh called itself the League for the Independence of Vietnam.

47753.q: On what date did Hồ Chí Minh proclaim the independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam in Hanoi?
47753.e: On 2 September 1945, shortly after Japan’s surrender, Hồ Chí Minh read out the declaration of independence in Hanoi. France did not recognise it, which led to the Indochina War.
47753.m: On 2 September 1945 Hồ Chí Minh proclaimed the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.

47754.q: What is the war called that the Việt Minh fought against France from 1946 to 1954?
47754.e: The Indochina War, also called the First Indochina War, lasted from 1946 to 1954. It ended with France withdrawing from Indochina.
47754.m: In the Indochina War the Việt Minh fought the colonial power France.

47755.q: Which occupying power did the Việt Minh fight in Indochina during the Second World War?
47755.e: Japan occupied Indochina from 1940 and took full control in March 1945. The Việt Minh used Japan’s surrender in August 1945 to seize power.
47755.m: In the Second World War the Việt Minh fought the Japanese occupiers.

47756.q: Which general led the Việt Minh troops in the Battle of Điện Biên Phủ?
47756.e: Võ Nguyên Giáp was the military commander-in-chief of the Việt Minh. His victory in 1954 made him one of the best-known strategists of the 20th century.
47756.m: General Võ Nguyên Giáp won at Điện Biên Phủ in 1954.

47757.q: During which period did the Battle of Điện Biên Phủ take place?
47757.e: The battle began on 13 March 1954 and ended on 7 May 1954 with the surrender of the French garrison. So it lasted almost two months.
47757.m: The Battle of Điện Biên Phủ lasted from March to May 1954.

47758.q: Which tactical factor contributed greatly to the French defeat at Điện Biên Phủ?
a: Lack of support from the navy
The closure of the Suez Canal
47758.e: The French had built their base in a valley basin. The Việt Minh dragged guns up the surrounding hills and could fire on the airstrip and the positions.
47758.m: The Việt Minh shelled Điện Biên Phủ from the surrounding hills.

47759.q: How was the surrounded French garrison at Điện Biên Phủ mainly supplied?
a: By air, with planes and parachutes
Via a secure road from Laos
47759.e: The base lay cut off in a valley basin and depended on the airstrip and parachute drops. When the Việt Minh put the airstrip under fire, supplies collapsed.
47759.m: Điện Biên Phủ depended on an airlift, which the Việt Minh cut off.

47760.q: Which conference decided the future of Indochina in 1954 after the Battle of Điện Biên Phủ?
47760.e: At the 1954 Geneva Conference on Indochina, Vietnam was provisionally divided at the 17th parallel. This made Switzerland host to an important Cold War meeting.
47760.m: In 1954 the Geneva Conference on Indochina divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel.

47761.q: Which economic problem marked Vietnam just before Đổi mới was introduced?
a: Inflation of several hundred per cent
A currency that was too strong
47761.e: In the mid-1980s Vietnam suffered from hyperinflation, food shortages and the effects of the planned economy. This crisis forced the party to reform.
47761.m: Before Đổi mới Vietnam suffered from extremely high inflation.

47762.q: Which Southeast Asian association of states did Vietnam join in 1995?
47762.e: Vietnam became a member of ASEAN in July 1995. Joining showed how the country opened up in foreign policy after Đổi mới.
47762.m: Vietnam has been a member of ASEAN since 1995.

47763.q: What term does Vietnam use for the economic model that came out of Đổi mới?
47763.e: Officially Vietnam speaks of a socialist-oriented market economy. Private companies and the market are allowed, but the Communist Party keeps its monopoly on political power.
47763.m: Vietnam calls its model a socialist-oriented market economy.

47764.q: What does the Vietnamese word “Đổi mới” mean?
47764.e: With Đổi mới the Communist Party began a renewal of the economy in 1986. Markets and private businesses were allowed, but the party kept power.

47765.q: What effect did the Đổi mới farming reforms have on Vietnam’s rice growing?
a: Vietnam became a major rice exporter
Vietnam had to import rice permanently
47765.e: Once farming families could decide about their harvest themselves again, production rose sharply. Vietnam went from importing rice to being one of the world’s biggest rice exporters.
47765.m: Thanks to Đổi mới, Vietnam became a major rice exporter.

47766.q: Which neighbouring country did Vietnam invade at the end of 1978, leaving it internationally isolated until it withdrew in 1989?
47766.e: Vietnam overthrew the Khmer Rouge regime in Cambodia and stayed in the country for over ten years. Only after withdrawing in 1989 could Vietnam open up in foreign policy.
47766.m: The withdrawal from Cambodia in 1989 made it easier for Vietnam to open up.

47767.q: In which year did Vietnam join the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
47767.e: Vietnam became a member of the WTO in January 2007. Joining was a milestone of the economic opening since Đổi mới.
47767.m: Vietnam has been a member of the WTO since 2007.

47768.q: Which Chinese reform policy is Đổi mới often compared with?
47768.e: Like China’s reform and opening up under Deng Xiaoping from 1978, Đổi mới combined a market economy with the sole rule of the party. Both countries remained one-party states.
47768.m: Đổi mới is similar to China’s reform and opening up under Deng Xiaoping.

47769.q: What does the name “Pathet Lao” mean?
47769.e: Pathet Lao literally means Land of the Lao. This is what the communist-led movement in Laos called itself.
47769.m: Pathet Lao means Land of the Lao.

47770.q: Which war in a neighbouring country shaped the Pathet Lao’s struggle most?
47770.e: The Pathet Lao fought closely alongside North Vietnam. Supplies for the Vietnam War ran through Laos, so the country was drawn heavily into the war.
47770.m: The Pathet Lao’s struggle was closely linked to the Vietnam War.

47771.q: Which force was the Pathet Lao most closely linked with militarily and politically?
47771.e: The Pathet Lao was formed with the help of the Việt Minh and later supported by North Vietnam. North Vietnamese troops also fought in Laos.
47771.m: The Pathet Lao was closely linked with North Vietnam.

47772.q: In which year did the Pathet Lao take power and abolish the monarchy in Laos?
47772.e: In December 1975 King Savang Vatthana abdicated and the Lao People’s Democratic Republic was proclaimed. In the same year the communists also won in Vietnam and Cambodia.
47772.m: The Pathet Lao came to power in Laos in 1975.

47773.q: How many parties are allowed in Laos today?
47773.e: Since 1975 the Lao People’s Revolutionary Party, which grew out of the Pathet Lao, has governed. It is still (as of 2026) the only party allowed.
47773.m: Laos is still a one-party state today.

47774.q: What has the official name of Laos been since the Pathet Lao took power in 1975?
47774.e: After the king abdicated, the People’s Democratic Republic was proclaimed in December 1975. The country still has this name today.
47774.m: Since 1975 Laos has been a people’s republic.

47775.q: Which intelligence agency supported the Pathet Lao’s opponents in Laos in the so-called Secret War?
47775.e: The USA fought a war in Laos that was never officially declared. The CIA armed mainly Hmong fighters against the Pathet Lao.
47775.m: The CIA waged a Secret War in Laos against the Pathet Lao.

47776.q: Which important North Vietnamese supply route ran through the area controlled by the Pathet Lao?
47776.e: Large parts of the Ho Chi Minh Trail ran through eastern Laos. That is why the USA bombed Laos very heavily; relative to its population, it is considered the most heavily bombed country.
47776.m: The Ho Chi Minh Trail ran through Pathet Lao areas in Laos.

47777.q: Which dictator fled Cuba on 1 January 1959?
47777.e: Fulgencio Batista left Cuba on New Year’s Eve 1959. With that, the Cuban Revolution had won.

47778.q: After which event did Fidel Castro name his “26th of July Movement”?
a: The attack on the Moncada Barracks in 1953
The landing of the Granma in 1956
The founding of the Rebel Army in 1957
47778.e: On 26 July 1953 Castro and his followers attacked the Moncada Barracks in Santiago de Cuba. The attack failed but gave the movement its name.
47778.m: The 26th of July Movement recalls the attack on the Moncada Barracks.

47779.q: With which text did Fidel Castro defend himself in court after the Moncada attack?
47779.e: Castro’s 1953 defence speech became known under the title “History Will Absolve Me”. It later served as the movement’s programme.
47779.m: Castro’s defence speech is called “History Will Absolve Me”.

47780.q: On which boat did Fidel Castro and his rebels land in Cuba in December 1956?
47780.e: The yacht Granma brought 82 rebels from Mexico to Cuba. After the landing most of them were killed or captured.
47780.m: Castro’s rebels landed in Cuba on the yacht Granma in 1956.

47781.q: In which mountain range did the rebels set up their guerrilla base from 1957?
47781.e: The Sierra Maestra in south-eastern Cuba gave the rebels shelter. From there they expanded the guerrilla war.
47781.m: The Cuban rebels fought from the Sierra Maestra.

47782.q: Which popular rebel commander vanished without trace on a flight in October 1959?
47782.e: Camilo Cienfuegos was one of the most popular leaders of the revolution. His small plane disappeared over the sea in October 1959.
47782.m: Camilo Cienfuegos vanished without trace on a flight in 1959.

47783.q: Which battle led by Che Guevara decided the rebels’ victory at the end of 1958?
47783.e: At the end of December 1958 Guevara’s troops captured Santa Clara and took control of one of Batista’s armoured trains. Shortly afterwards Batista fled.
47783.m: Che Guevara decided the war by capturing Santa Clara.

47784.q: Which major reform did the revolutionary government pass in May 1959?
47784.e: The first agrarian reform law limited land ownership and expropriated large estates, including those of US companies. This sharpened the conflict with the USA.
47784.m: In May 1959 a major agrarian reform began in Cuba.

47785.q: In which year did the Bay of Pigs invasion take place?
47785.e: The landing began on 17 April 1961. After about three days the invasion had failed.
47785.m: The Bay of Pigs invasion failed in April 1961.

47786.q: Which US agency planned the Bay of Pigs invasion and trained the Cuban exiles for it?
47786.e: The CIA intelligence agency trained the Cuban exiles and planned the landing. Officially, US involvement was meant to stay hidden.
47786.m: The CIA planned the Bay of Pigs invasion.

47787.q: Who landed in Cuba at the Bay of Pigs in April 1961?
a: Cuban exiles trained by the USA
47787.e: About 1,400 Cuban exiles of Brigade 2506 landed on Cuba’s south coast. The USA wanted to hide its involvement and therefore sent no ground troops of its own.
47787.m: Cuban exiles trained by the USA landed at the Bay of Pigs.

47788.q: Which US President gave the order for the Bay of Pigs invasion?
47788.e: The plan was drawn up under Eisenhower, but Kennedy gave the order in April 1961. Afterwards he publicly took responsibility for the failure.
47788.m: In 1961 President Kennedy had the Bay of Pigs invasion carried out.

47789.q: On which beach in the Bay of Pigs did the main fighting take place?
47789.e: In Cuba the event is named after Playa Girón beach. The invaders landed there and at Playa Larga.
47789.m: In Cuba the invasion is named after Playa Girón beach.

47790.q: How were the captured Bay of Pigs invaders freed at the end of 1962?
a: In exchange for food and medicines
Through a prisoner exchange with the USSR
Through a general amnesty by Castro
47790.e: Cuba released the more than 1,100 prisoners in December 1962. In return it received food and medicines worth about 53 million dollars.
47790.m: The Bay of Pigs prisoners were released in exchange for food and medicines.

47791.q: What political consequence did the Bay of Pigs invasion have for Cuba?
a: Cuba moved closer to the USSR
47791.e: On the eve of the fighting Castro declared the revolution socialist. Afterwards Cuba sought even more protection from the Soviet Union, which contributed to the Cuban Missile Crisis.
47791.m: After the Bay of Pigs, Cuba tied itself more closely to the Soviet Union.

47792.q: Which CIA director had to leave office after the Bay of Pigs fiasco?
47792.e: Allen Dulles shared responsibility for the operation. Kennedy replaced him with John McCone at the end of 1961.
47792.m: CIA director Allen Dulles lost his job after the Bay of Pigs.

47793.q: How did the USA discover the Soviet missile sites in Cuba in October 1962?
a: Aerial photos from a U-2 spy plane
47793.e: On 14 October 1962 a U-2 plane photographed launch pads in Cuba. The analysis of the pictures set off the crisis.
47793.m: In 1962 a U-2 spy plane photographed the missiles in Cuba.

47794.q: According to the usual count, how many days did the Cuban Missile Crisis last?
47794.e: It is counted from 16 October 1962, when Kennedy saw the aerial photos, to 28 October 1962, when Moscow agreed to withdraw the missiles. That is why people speak of the thirteen days.
47794.m: The Cuban Missile Crisis lasted thirteen days.

47795.q: Which agreement did the USA, the USSR and Great Britain sign in 1963, partly as a result of the Cuban Missile Crisis?
a: Treaty banning nuclear tests in the atmosphere
47795.e: The 1963 treaty banned nuclear weapons tests in the atmosphere, in space and under water. Underground tests remained allowed.
47795.m: Since 1963 nuclear tests in the atmosphere have been banned by treaty.

47796.q: What secret promise did the USA make to settle the Cuban Missile Crisis?
a: Withdrawing the Jupiter missiles from Turkey
47796.e: Publicly the USA promised not to attack Cuba. Secretly it also agreed to withdraw its Jupiter missiles from Turkey.
47796.m: After the Cuban Missile Crisis the USA withdrew its Jupiter missiles from Turkey.

47797.q: Which country represented US interests in Havana during the Cuban Missile Crisis?
47797.e: After relations were broken off in 1961, Switzerland took on the protecting power mandate for the USA in Cuba. It kept it until 2015.
47797.m: From 1961 to 2015 Switzerland represented US interests in Cuba.

47798.q: Which direct link did the USA and the USSR set up in 1963 as a lesson from the Cuban Missile Crisis?
47798.e: The “hotline” connected Washington and Moscow directly by teleprinter. This was meant to clear up misunderstandings faster in a crisis.
47798.m: Since 1963 the hotline has linked Washington and Moscow.

47799.q: Which Soviet officer prevented the launch of a nuclear torpedo from a submarine during the Cuban Missile Crisis?
47799.e: On submarine B-59 the use of the nuclear weapon had to be agreed unanimously. Vasily Arkhipov voted against it and so possibly prevented a nuclear war.
47799.m: In 1962 Vasily Arkhipov prevented the launch of a nuclear torpedo.

a: A U-2 plane was shot down over Cuba
47800.e: On this day a US spy plane was shot down over Cuba and the pilot was killed. The danger of war was at its greatest that day.
47800.m: On Black Saturday a U-2 plane was shot down over Cuba.

47801.q: Why did the Soviet Union station nuclear missiles in Cuba in 1962?
a: To protect Cuba and counter the US missiles in Turkey
To launch satellites into space from Cuba
To force Mexico into an alliance
To make Cuba break off relations with China
47801.e: After the Bay of Pigs invasion, Cuba feared a new attack. Khrushchev also wanted a counterweight to the American missiles in Turkey. The action was called Operation Anadyr.
47801.m: With the missiles in Cuba, Moscow was also responding to US missiles in Turkey.

47802.q: Which event triggered the “Special Period in Time of Peace” in Cuba from 1990?
a: The collapse of the Soviet Union
47802.e: With the end of the Eastern Bloc and the Soviet Union, Cuba lost its most important trading partners and subsidies. The government then declared the Special Period.
47802.m: The collapse of the Soviet Union plunged Cuba into the Special Period.

47803.q: By roughly how much did Cuba’s economic output shrink at the start of the Special Period?
47803.e: Gross domestic product fell by about 35 per cent by the mid-1990s. There was a shortage above all of oil, spare parts and food.
47803.m: In the Special Period Cuba’s economy shrank by about a third.

47804.q: Which means of transport did Cuba buy from China by the million during the Special Period because of the fuel shortage?
47804.e: Cuba bought about 1.2 million bicycles from China. Because there was no petrol, they replaced cars and buses in many places.
47804.m: In the Special Period many Cubans rode bicycles.

47805.q: What are the urban vegetable gardens called that appeared in Cuba during the Special Period?
47805.e: Because fertilisers and pesticides were lacking, organic gardens called organopónicos were set up in the cities. They helped secure the supply of vegetables.
47805.m: In the Special Period Cubans grew vegetables in organopónicos.

47806.q: Which 1996 US law tightened the embargo against Cuba during the Special Period?
47806.e: The 1996 Helms-Burton Act also threatened foreign companies that invested in Cuba. The Torricelli Act had already tightened the embargo in 1992.
47806.m: In 1996 the Helms-Burton Act tightened the embargo against Cuba.

47807.q: Which branch of the economy was expanded into Cuba’s most important new source of foreign currency during the Special Period?
47807.e: Cuba opened up to foreign tourists and hotel investment. Tourism brought urgently needed foreign currency into the country.
47807.m: In the Special Period Cuba relied heavily on tourism.

47808.q: What were the Cubans called who fled towards the USA on home-made rafts in 1994?
47808.e: After protests in Havana in August 1994, the government let people leave. Tens of thousands risked the dangerous crossing on rafts (balsa in Spanish). The Marielitos, by contrast, had come by boat in 1980.
47808.m: The balseros fled Cuba on rafts in 1994.

47809.q: Which country helped Cuba out of the Special Period crisis with cheap oil deliveries from 2000?
47809.e: Under President Hugo Chávez, Venezuela supplied oil on favourable terms from 2000. In return Cuba sent doctors, among other things.
47809.m: From 2000 Venezuela supported Cuba with cheap oil.

47810.q: Who is the Sandinista National Liberation Front in Nicaragua named after?
47810.e: Augusto César Sandino fought against the US occupation of Nicaragua from 1927 to 1933. He was murdered in 1934 and is regarded as a national hero.
47810.m: The Sandinistas are named after Augusto César Sandino.

47811.q: Which revolution was the model for the founders of the Sandinista National Liberation Front?
47811.e: The FSLN was founded in 1961, shortly after Fidel Castro’s victory. Like the Cuban rebels, it relied on guerrilla warfare.
47811.m: The Sandinistas took the Cuban Revolution as their model.

47812.q: Which family dictatorship did the Sandinistas overthrow in Nicaragua in 1979?
47812.e: On 19 July 1979 the Sandinistas entered Managua after Anastasio Somoza Debayle had fled. The Somoza family had ruled since the 1930s.
47812.m: In 1979 the Sandinistas ended the rule of the Somoza family.

47813.q: What were the US-backed rebels called who fought against the Sandinistas in the 1980s?
47813.e: The Contras operated mainly from Honduras. Their secret funding through arms sales to Iran became known as the Iran-Contra affair.
47813.m: The Contras fought the Sandinistas with US help.

47814.q: Which large education programme did the Sandinistas carry out in 1980?
47814.e: In the 1980 literacy campaign, young volunteers taught reading and writing throughout the country. The share of people who could not read fell considerably.
47814.m: In 1980 the Sandinistas fought illiteracy with a large campaign.

47815.q: Who beat the Sandinistas in the 1990 presidential election?
47815.e: Violeta Barrios de Chamorro won in 1990 as the candidate of an opposition alliance. Daniel Ortega handed over power peacefully.
47815.m: In 1990 Violeta Chamorro defeated the Sandinistas.

47816.q: Which Sandinista has been President of Nicaragua again since 2007 (as of 2026)?
47816.e: Daniel Ortega had already been President from 1985 to 1990 and returned to office in 2007. Since 2025 he has shared the office with his wife Rosario Murillo as co-president and rules in an increasingly authoritarian way.
47816.m: Daniel Ortega has ruled Nicaragua since 2007.

47817.q: Which rebel group fought Nicaragua’s Sandinista government with US support in the 1980s?
47817.e: The Contras were funded and trained by the USA. In their war against the Sandinistas, the aid worker Maurice Demierre from Fribourg was also killed in 1986.
47817.m: The Contras fought the Sandinistas with US help.

47818.q: Which court ruled against the USA in 1986 for supporting the Contras and mining Nicaraguan harbours?
47818.e: In the Nicaragua case, the International Court of Justice in The Hague ruled that the USA had broken international law. The USA did not accept the ruling.
47818.m: In 1986 the International Court of Justice ruled against the USA in the Nicaragua case.

47819.q: Which politician won Chile’s presidential election in 1970 as the Unidad Popular candidate?
47819.e: Salvador Allende received the most votes in 1970 and was confirmed by Congress. He was seen as the first freely elected Marxist president in Latin America.
47819.m: In 1970 Salvador Allende became President for Unidad Popular.

47820.q: Roughly what share of the vote did Allende receive in the 1970 presidential election?
47820.e: Allende got about 36 per cent of the vote and was narrowly ahead. Because nobody had an absolute majority, Congress decided.
47820.m: In 1970 Allende won with just over a third of the vote.

47821.q: What did Unidad Popular call its aim of introducing socialism by democratic means?
47821.e: Allende wanted to achieve socialism through elections and laws, not through armed revolution. People spoke of the Chilean road to socialism.
47821.m: Unidad Popular wanted a Chilean road to socialism.

47822.q: Which important raw material did the Allende government nationalise in 1971?
47822.e: In 1971 Congress voted unanimously to nationalise the large copper mines. The expropriated US companies received hardly any compensation.
47822.m: In 1971 Allende nationalised Chile’s copper mining.

47823.q: Which occupational group brought Chile’s supplies to a standstill with a nationwide strike in October 1972?
47823.e: The lorry owners’ strike in October 1972 paralysed transport across the whole country. It made the economic crisis under Unidad Popular worse.
47823.m: In 1972 lorry owners went on strike against the Allende government.

47824.q: Which economic problem reached extreme levels under Unidad Popular in 1973?
47824.e: In 1973 price rises reached several hundred per cent. On top of that there were empty shops and black markets.
47824.m: Under Unidad Popular, inflation rose to several hundred per cent in 1973.

47825.q: Which general led the military coup against Unidad Popular on 11 September 1973?
47825.e: Augusto Pinochet had only just become commander-in-chief of the army. After the coup he ruled Chile as a dictator until 1990.
47825.m: In 1973 Augusto Pinochet overthrew the Unidad Popular government.

47826.q: Where did Salvador Allende die on the day of the 1973 coup?
47826.e: La Moneda presidential palace was bombed by fighter planes. Allende died there; investigations confirmed suicide.
47826.m: In 1973 Salvador Allende died in La Moneda presidential palace.

47827.q: What kind of government was the Derg, which ruled Ethiopia from 1974?
47827.e: The Derg was a council of officers that overthrew the emperor and rebuilt the country on the Soviet model. The word means “committee” or “council” in Ge’ez.
47827.m: The Derg was a Marxist military government.

47828.q: Which emperor did the Derg overthrow in Ethiopia in 1974?
47828.e: Haile Selassie was deposed in September 1974. He died in captivity in 1975, which ended the Ethiopian monarchy.
47828.m: In 1974 the Derg overthrew Emperor Haile Selassie.

47829.q: Who came out on top as ruler at the head of the Derg?
47829.e: Mengistu Haile Mariam eliminated his rivals in 1977 and became undisputed ruler. Aman Andom and Tafari Benti had been nominal heads of state before him.
47829.m: Mengistu Haile Mariam was the ruler of the Derg.

47830.q: What is the wave of persecution against the Derg’s political opponents in 1977 and 1978 called?
47830.e: In the Red Terror the regime had tens of thousands of suspected opponents killed. Mengistu was later convicted of genocide for this in Ethiopia.
47830.m: The Derg’s Red Terror cost tens of thousands of lives.

47831.q: Against which neighbouring country did Ethiopia under the Derg fight the Ogaden War in 1977 and 1978?
47831.e: Somalia wanted to conquer the Ogaden region, which is inhabited by Somalis. With the help of the Soviet Union and Cuban troops, Ethiopia won.
47831.m: In the Ogaden War Ethiopia fought against Somalia.

47832.q: Which charity concert drew attention to the famine in Ethiopia under the Derg in 1985?
47832.e: Live Aid took place in London and Philadelphia in July 1985 and raised money for the starving. The famine was made worse by drought, war and the regime’s policies.
47832.m: In 1985 Live Aid raised money against the famine in Ethiopia.

47833.q: Which measure did the Derg take in the countryside in 1975?
47833.e: With the 1975 land reform, all rural land was nationalised. Farmers received the right to use it but not ownership.
47833.m: In 1975 the Derg nationalised all rural land.

47834.q: Which country did Mengistu Haile Mariam flee to when the regime fell in 1991?
47834.e: In May 1991 Mengistu fled to Zimbabwe, where he was granted asylum. Shortly afterwards the EPRDF rebels took Addis Ababa.

47835.q: Why was Mozambique’s FRELIMO founded in neighbouring Tanzania in 1962?
a: Because Mozambique was still a Portuguese colony
Because Tanzania governed Mozambique at that time
Because the UN had decided so
Because there was a civil war in Mozambique
47835.e: In the Portuguese colony, independence movements were banned. So in 1962 several groups joined together in exile in Dar es Salaam.
47835.m: FRELIMO was founded in exile in Tanzania in 1962.

47836.q: Who was the first President of FRELIMO?
47836.e: Eduardo Mondlane had studied in the USA and had been taught at Swiss Mission schools in Mozambique. He led FRELIMO until he was murdered in 1969.
47836.m: Eduardo Mondlane was the first President of FRELIMO.

47837.q: How was FRELIMO founder Eduardo Mondlane killed in 1969?
47837.e: Mondlane died in Dar es Salaam in February 1969 when a book containing a bomb exploded. The culprits were never clearly identified.
47837.m: Eduardo Mondlane was killed by a parcel bomb in 1969.

47838.q: In which year did Mozambique become independent under FRELIMO’s leadership?
47838.e: After the Carnation Revolution in Portugal in 1974, Mozambique became independent on 25 June 1975. Samora Machel became the first President.

47839.q: Which rebel movement did the FRELIMO government fight in the civil war from 1977 to 1992?
47839.e: RENAMO was supported first by Rhodesia and later by South Africa. The war cost hundreds of thousands of lives.
47839.m: In the civil war FRELIMO fought against RENAMO.

47840.q: In which city was the 1992 peace agreement between FRELIMO and RENAMO signed?
47840.e: The General Peace Agreement was signed in Rome in October 1992. The mediation was mainly done by the Catholic Community of Sant’Egidio.
47840.m: The civil war in Mozambique ended in 1992 with a peace agreement in Rome.

47841.q: How did Mozambique’s first President Samora Machel die in 1986?
47841.e: Machel’s plane crashed near Mbuzini in South Africa in October 1986. The exact cause is still disputed today.
47841.m: Samora Machel died in a plane crash in 1986.

47842.q: What ideological change did FRELIMO make in 1989?
a: It brought back the planned economy
47842.e: In 1989 FRELIMO dropped Marxism-Leninism as its guiding principle. In 1990 Mozambique got a constitution with a multi-party system.

47843.q: Who was Angola’s first President and leader of the MPLA?
47843.e: Agostinho Neto, a doctor and poet, led the MPLA to independence. He was President from 1975 until his death in 1979.
47843.m: Agostinho Neto was Angola’s first President.

47844.q: When did Angola become independent under the MPLA?
47844.e: The MPLA proclaimed independence in Luanda on 11 November 1975. At the same time the fight with its rivals FNLA and UNITA was already raging.

47845.q: Which event in Portugal cleared the way for Angola’s independence in 1974?
47845.e: The Carnation Revolution of 25 April 1974 overthrew the dictatorship in Portugal. The new government ended the colonial wars in Africa.
47845.m: After the Carnation Revolution, Portugal let its colonies go.

47846.q: Who led UNITA, the MPLA’s main opponent in the Angolan civil war?
47846.e: Jonas Savimbi founded UNITA in 1966. It was supported by South Africa and at times by the USA.
47846.m: Jonas Savimbi led UNITA against the MPLA.

47847.q: Which country sent tens of thousands of soldiers to Angola from 1975 to support the MPLA?
47847.e: From 1975 Cuba intervened with Operation Carlota. Cuban troops stayed in the country until 1991.
47847.m: From 1975 Cuban troops fought for the MPLA in Angola.

47848.q: Which neighbouring country of Angola became independent after the 1988 peace agreements?
47848.e: After the Battle of Cuito Cuanavale, Angola, Cuba and South Africa reached agreement in 1988. South Africa withdrew from Namibia, which became independent in 1990.
47848.m: The end of the war in Angola paved the way for Namibia’s independence in 1990.

47849.q: Which event ended the Angolan civil war in 2002?
47849.e: UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi was killed in combat in February 2002. A few weeks later the MPLA government and UNITA agreed a ceasefire.
47849.m: After Savimbi’s death, the civil war in Angola ended in 2002.

47850.q: Which MPLA politician governed Angola as President from 1979 to 2017?
47850.e: José Eduardo dos Santos succeeded Agostinho Neto in 1979 and governed for 38 years. In 2017 João Lourenço took over.
47850.m: José Eduardo dos Santos governed Angola from 1979 to 2017.

47851.q: In which year did US President Harry S. Truman announce the doctrine named after him?
47851.e: Truman gave his keynote speech in March 1947. It is seen as one of the starting points of the Cold War.
47851.m: The Truman Doctrine dates from spring 1947.

47852.q: According to Truman’s speech of March 1947, whom should the USA support?
a: All states that supply raw materials to the USA
Only members of the United Nations
Former colonies on the way to independence
47852.e: Truman promised help to free peoples resisting subjugation by armed minorities or outside pressure. He meant mainly communist influence.
47852.m: The Truman Doctrine promised free peoples support against subjugation.

47853.q: Which conflict was raging in Greece in 1947 when Truman announced his doctrine?
a: A civil war against communist partisans
A war of independence against Italy
An uprising against British colonial rule
47853.e: In Greece the government fought communist-led partisans from 1946 to 1949. The USA feared a communist takeover.
47853.m: The Greek Civil War was one reason for the Truman Doctrine.

47854.q: Which Soviet demand put Turkey under pressure before the Truman Doctrine?
a: Joint control over the Bosporus and Dardanelles
47854.e: After 1945 Moscow demanded a say and bases at the Turkish Straits. The USA wanted to strengthen Turkey against this pressure.
47854.m: After 1945 the Soviet Union wanted a say over the Turkish Straits.

47855.q: Which aid programme for Western Europe followed the Truman Doctrine in 1948?
47855.e: With the Marshall Plan the USA helped rebuild Western Europe, partly to contain the influence of communism. Switzerland was also one of the participating states.
47855.m: The Truman Doctrine was followed by the Marshall Plan in 1948.

47856.q: How did the Greek Civil War, in which the USA had intervened under the Truman Doctrine, end in 1949?
a: With victory for the government troops
47856.e: With American help the Greek government won in 1949. Greece stayed in the western camp and joined NATO in 1952.
47856.m: Thanks to American help, Greece stayed in the western camp.

47857.q: Which country had announced in early 1947 that it could no longer provide support to Greece and Turkey?
47857.e: Economically weakened Great Britain withdrew from its protective role. The USA stepped into the gap with the Truman Doctrine.
47857.m: In 1947 the USA took over Britain’s former role in the eastern Mediterranean.

47858.q: Which traditional stance of US foreign policy did the Truman Doctrine finally break with?
47858.e: The USA committed itself to supporting “free peoples” worldwide. With this it gave up its reluctance to get involved in conflicts outside the Americas.
47858.m: With the Truman Doctrine the USA became a protecting power that intervened worldwide.

47859.q: What did the USA provide billions of dollars for with the Marshall Plan from 1948?
a: Independence of the colonies in Africa
47859.e: Through the European Recovery Program about 13 billion dollars flowed to Europe by 1952. In the USA the money was managed by the Economic Cooperation Administration.
47859.m: The Marshall Plan helped rebuild Western Europe.

47860.q: What happened to the money that European importers paid in their own currency for Marshall Plan goods?
a: It went into funds for investment in their own country
It was sent back to the USA
It was destroyed to curb inflation
It went to the United Nations
47860.e: The payments in national currency formed so-called counterpart funds. These were used to give loans for reconstruction and investment.
47860.m: The counterpart funds more or less doubled the effect of Marshall Plan aid.

47861.q: Which Soviet foreign minister walked out of the Paris conference on the Marshall Plan in July 1947?
47861.e: Molotov rejected joint planning because Moscow feared control by the West. After that the whole Eastern Bloc stayed out of the programme.
47861.m: With Molotov’s departure from Paris, Europe was economically divided in 1947.

47862.q: Which information bureau did the Soviet Union and other communist parties found in September 1947, partly in response to the Marshall Plan?
47862.e: From 1947 the Communist Information Bureau (Cominform) coordinated Europe’s communist parties. The Comintern had already been dissolved in 1943.
47862.m: In 1947 the Soviet Union brought the communist parties together in the Cominform.

47863.q: Apart from containment, which economic self-interest did the USA pursue with the Marshall Plan?
47863.e: A prosperous Europe could buy American goods. Much of the aid money was also used for purchases in the USA.
47863.m: The Marshall Plan also benefited the American export economy.

47864.q: Which Eastern European country at first wanted to take part in the Marshall Plan in 1947 but had to pull out under pressure from Moscow?
47864.e: The Prague government first agreed to take part. After a meeting with Stalin it withdrew its acceptance.
47864.m: Moscow banned Czechoslovakia from taking part in the Marshall Plan.

47865.q: What position did George C. Marshall hold during the Second World War?
a: Chief of Staff of the US Army
47865.e: Marshall was Chief of Staff of the US Army from 1939 to 1945. The Supreme Commander of the Allied forces in Europe, on the other hand, was Dwight D. Eisenhower.
47865.m: In the Second World War George C. Marshall was the US Army’s top general.

47866.q: Which country received the largest share of Marshall Plan aid?
47866.e: Great Britain got the most, with over 3 billion dollars, ahead of France. West Germany received considerably less but benefited greatly.
47866.m: Most Marshall Plan money went to Great Britain.

47867.q: Which US President coined the image of falling dominoes at a press conference in 1954?
47867.e: In April 1954 Eisenhower compared the countries of Southeast Asia to a row of dominoes: if the first one falls, the others quickly follow.
47867.m: Eisenhower made the domino image famous in 1954.

47868.q: Which region of the world did the domino theory mainly refer to?
47868.e: It was feared that after Indochina, Thailand, Malaya, Indonesia and other Southeast Asian states would also become communist.
47868.m: The domino theory was mainly about Southeast Asia.

47869.q: What is the core idea of the domino theory?
a: If one country becomes communist, its neighbours will follow
47869.e: The theory assumed a chain reaction: a communist takeover in one country would spread to the neighbouring countries.
47869.m: The domino theory expected a chain reaction of takeovers.

47870.q: Which 1954 defeat of which colonial power gave the domino theory special urgency?
47870.e: In May 1954 France was defeated by the Viet Minh at Dien Bien Phu. This ended French rule in Indochina.
47870.m: In 1954 Dien Bien Phu sealed the end of French Indochina.

47871.q: Which military alliance did the USA and its partners found in 1954 to support further “dominoes”?
47871.e: The Southeast Asia Treaty Organization (SEATO) was founded in Manila in September 1954. ASEAN, on the other hand, is an association of states from 1967 with no military obligation to assist.
47871.m: SEATO was the NATO-like answer to the fear of dominoes in Asia.

47872.q: Which war was justified by several US governments with the domino theory?
47872.e: Kennedy and Johnson justified the growing involvement in Vietnam by saying that the fall of South Vietnam would endanger all of Southeast Asia.
47872.m: The domino theory served as a justification for the Vietnam War.

47873.q: Which two neighbouring countries came under communist rule together with South Vietnam in 1975?
47873.e: In 1975 communist movements took power in Laos and Cambodia. Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia, however, did not follow, which critics point to against the theory.
47873.m: In 1975 the dominoes fell only in Indochina.

47874.q: To which region did Ronald Reagan’s government apply the domino argument in the 1980s?
47874.e: Reagan warned that after Nicaragua, other Central American states such as El Salvador could become communist. He used this to justify supporting anti-communist forces.
47874.m: In the 1980s the domino argument was applied to Central America.

47875.q: Which party did Senator Joseph McCarthy belong to?
47875.e: The Republican Joseph McCarthy was a senator for Wisconsin from 1947 until his death in 1957. He led an aggressive hunt for supposed communists.
47875.m: Joseph McCarthy was a Republican senator.

47876.q: In his speech in Wheeling in February 1950, in which government department did McCarthy claim to know of many communists?
47876.e: McCarthy claimed to have a list of names of communists in the State Department. He never produced any evidence.
47876.m: McCarthy’s rise began with unproven accusations against the State Department.

47877.q: What was the group of screenwriters and directors called who refused to testify before Congress in 1947 and were convicted?
47877.e: The Hollywood Ten invoked freedom of speech and were sentenced to prison for contempt of Congress.
47877.m: The Hollywood Ten became the symbol of the hunt for communists in the film industry.

47878.q: Which committee of the House of Representatives questioned artists from 1947 about alleged communist links?
47878.e: The House Un-American Activities Committee (HUAC) investigated “un-American activities”. It asked witnesses: “Are you now or have you ever been a member of the Communist Party?”
47878.m: HUAC questioned suspects about alleged communist links.

47879.q: Why were Julius and Ethel Rosenberg executed in the USA in 1953?
a: Atomic spying for the Soviet Union
47879.e: The couple were convicted of passing secrets about the atomic bomb to the Soviet Union. The verdict was controversial even at the time.
47879.m: The Rosenberg case shows the fear of spies in the early 1950s.

47880.q: Which 1953 play by Arthur Miller about the Salem witch trials is seen as an allegory of the McCarthy era?
47880.e: In “The Crucible” Miller shows how fear and denunciation destroy a community. Miller himself later had to testify before HUAC.
47880.m: Arthur Miller criticised the hunt for communists with a play about witch trials.

47881.q: What did the US Senate decide against Joseph McCarthy in December 1954?
47881.e: After the televised Army hearings, the Senate censured McCarthy by a large majority. After that he quickly lost influence.
47881.m: The Senate’s censure in 1954 ended McCarthy’s power.

47882.q: What is the practice called of no longer employing suspected artists in the film industry?
47882.e: The so-called blacklist named hundreds of people who no longer got any work. Some carried on working under false names.
47882.m: The blacklist cost many artists in Hollywood their jobs.

47883.q: Which television journalist criticised McCarthy on his programme “See It Now” in March 1954?
47883.e: Edward R. Murrow showed McCarthy through his own statements and contradictions. The programme contributed to the senator’s loss of reputation.
47883.m: In 1954 television helped to expose McCarthy.

47884.q: What was the parliamentary commission of inquiry (PUK) actually investigating when it came across the secret files in 1989?
a: The Federal Prosecutor’s work against money laundering and drug trafficking
The purchase of new fighter jets
The finances of the federal pension fund
47884.e: The commission examined how the Federal Department of Justice and Police was run, especially regarding money laundering and drug trafficking. In doing so it discovered a large room full of files.
47884.m: The secret files were discovered more or less by chance during another investigation.

47885.q: Roughly how many people asked to see their file after the secret files scandal?
47885.e: Over 300,000 people made a request. Many received copies in which the names of third parties were blacked out.
47885.m: After 1989 hundreds of thousands wanted to know what the state had noted about them.

47886.q: Where are the state security files from before 1990 kept today?
a: In the West Wing of the Federal Palace
In the Swiss National Museum in Zurich
At the Office of the Attorney General
47886.e: The files were handed over to the Federal Archives in Bern. There they are used for historical research today.
47886.m: The secret files are now part of the Federal Archives.

47887.q: Which federal authority, with its political police, was responsible for the secret files?
47887.e: The political police was part of the Office of the Attorney General. For decades it collected information about supposed enemies of the state.
47887.m: The secret files came from the political police of the Office of the Attorney General.

47888.q: How did the people vote in 1998 on the initiative “S.o.S. Switzerland without snooping police”?
47888.e: The initiative wanted to abolish the political police. In June 1998 the people and the cantons rejected it by a large majority.
47888.m: In 1998 abolishing the political police did not win a majority.

47889.q: In which office was Elisabeth Kopp the first woman in Switzerland?
47889.e: In 1984 Elisabeth Kopp was elected as the first woman on the Federal Council and headed the Department of Justice and Police.
47889.m: In 1984 Elisabeth Kopp was Switzerland’s first female Federal Councillor.

47890.q: Why did Federal Councillor Elisabeth Kopp have to resign in January 1989?
a: She had warned her husband about investigations into a company
She had ordered files to be kept on members of parliament
She had signed a secret treaty with NATO
47890.e: Kopp advised her husband by phone to leave the board of a company that the Office of the Attorney General was investigating. At first she kept quiet about the phone call.
47890.m: A phone call she kept quiet about cost Elisabeth Kopp her office.

47891.q: Shortly after which world event was the commission’s report on the secret files published in November 1989?
a: The fall of the Berlin Wall
The end of the Gulf War
The break-up of the Soviet Union
47891.e: The report came out on 22 November 1989, almost two weeks after the fall of the Wall on 9 November. The fear of communism suddenly seemed out of date.
47891.m: The secret files scandal broke at the time of the fall of the Wall.

47892.q: How did the 1990 criminal case against Elisabeth Kopp for breaching official secrecy end?
a: With an acquittal by the Federal Supreme Court
With the case being dropped as time-barred
47892.e: The Federal Supreme Court acquitted Kopp in February 1990. However, her resignation could no longer be undone.
47892.m: Elisabeth Kopp was acquitted in the criminal case.

47893.q: Which political direction does the Swiss Party of Labour stand for?
47893.e: The PdA was founded in Basel in 1944 and brought together communists and left-wing socialists. It stands to the left of the Social Democratic Party.
47893.m: The Party of Labour is Switzerland’s communist party.

47894.q: Which party, a forerunner of the Party of Labour, did the Federal Council ban in November 1940?
47894.e: The Federal Council banned the Communist Party of Switzerland (KPS) in November 1940. Its members came together again in the PdA in 1944.
47894.m: The PdA is the successor to the KPS, banned in 1940.

47895.q: Why did the Party of Labour lose many votes after its good result in 1947?
a: Because of the Cold War and distrust of communists
Because it merged with the SVP
47895.e: In 1947 the PdA won seven seats in the National Council. With the Cold War, and especially after the Hungarian Uprising of 1956, many people saw communists as a danger, and the party lost heavily.
47895.m: In the Cold War the PdA lost many voters.

47896.q: Under what name does the Party of Labour stand in the cantons of Neuchâtel, Vaud and Jura?
47896.e: In these cantons the party is called Parti ouvrier populaire, POP for short. In French the national name is Parti suisse du Travail.
47896.m: In French-speaking Switzerland the PdA is known as the POP.

47897.q: Which towns in the canton of Neuchâtel are traditional strongholds of the Party of Labour?
47897.e: In the watchmaking towns of Le Locle and La Chaux-de-Fonds, with their large working class, the PdA is still well rooted today.
47897.m: The PdA is strong in the watchmaking towns of the Neuchâtel Jura.

47898.q: What is the German-language newspaper of the Party of Labour called?
47898.e: “Vorwärts” is the PdA’s paper. “Volksrecht” and “Berner Tagwacht” were social democratic papers.

47899.q: Which party did the Swiss communists, the forerunners of the Party of Labour, split from in 1921?
47899.e: After the Russian Revolution the SP argued about joining the Communist International. Those in favour founded the Communist Party of Switzerland in 1921.
47899.m: The Swiss communists split from the SP in 1921.

47900.q: Which body made up of social democrats and trade unions led the national general strike of 1918?
47900.e: The Olten Action Committee, founded in February 1918, linked the party and the trade unions. It called the strike and called it off.
47900.m: The Olten Action Committee led the national general strike.

47901.q: Who chaired the Olten Action Committee during the national general strike?
47901.e: The Bernese social democrat Robert Grimm was the leading figure of the committee. He is seen as the face of the national general strike.
47901.m: Robert Grimm was the head of the national general strike.

47902.q: Roughly how many people took part in the national general strike on the first day?
47902.e: On 12 November 1918 about 250,000 workers stopped work, especially in industry and on the railways.
47902.m: About a quarter of a million people went on strike in 1918.

47903.q: Which demand of the national general strike was only fulfilled in 1948?
a: Proportional representation for the National Council
New election of the National Council
47903.e: The AHV came into force on 1 January 1948, almost 30 years after the strike. The 48-hour week had already come in 1919 in the Factory Act.
47903.m: The AHV is a late result of the national general strike.

47904.q: In which town did soldiers shoot dead three young watch factory workers on 14 November 1918?
47904.e: In Grenchen three strikers aged 17 to 29 were killed. Nobody was convicted for it.
47904.m: The national general strike claimed three lives in Grenchen.

47905.q: Which general had already pushed for a large deployment of troops in the cities before the national general strike?
47905.e: Ulrich Wille was General of the Swiss Army in the First World War. He pushed for tough military action against the labour movement.
47905.m: In 1918 General Ulrich Wille relied on military toughness.

47906.q: What sentence was Robert Grimm given in the 1919 trial over the national general strike?
47906.e: The military court sentenced Robert Grimm, Fritz Platten and Friedrich Schneider to six months in prison each.
47906.m: In 1919 the strike leaders were each given six months in prison.

47907.q: Which international socialist conference did Robert Grimm organise in the canton of Bern in 1915?
47907.e: In 1915 opponents of the war from the socialist movement, including Lenin, met in Zimmerwald. Grimm was the organiser.
47907.m: In 1915 Robert Grimm brought the opponents of the war to Zimmerwald.

47908.q: On what day did the Hungarian Uprising begin with a student demonstration in Budapest?
47908.e: On 23 October 1956 students demonstrated in Budapest. After shots were fired into the crowd, armed fighting broke out.
47908.m: The Hungarian Uprising began on 23 October 1956.

47909.q: When did Soviet troops crush the Hungarian Uprising with a major offensive?
47909.e: On 4 November 1956 Soviet troops moved into Budapest. The fighting in the capital lasted about a week.
47909.m: At the start of November 1956 Soviet tanks crushed the uprising.

47910.q: Roughly how many Hungarian refugees did Switzerland take in after 1956?
